courses.name: Consumer Product Design

contentEvidence.description2: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.
contentEvidence.profile: Teaches consumer-product design and development through projects that progress from understanding an existing product to creating a new one. Students investigate product mechanisms and environmental impact, interview potential customers, translate needs into specifications, select concepts, and develop production plans and prototypes where feasible. The final project integrates these stages with industrial scaling and elementary economic analysis. Sustainability, including material use, repairability, lifespan and circularity, informs design decisions throughout.

courses.name: Decision-making in AI

contentEvidence.description2: Introduces planning techniques for AI systems in deterministic and non‑deterministic environments. Addresses uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and optimizing behaviour under constraints.

judgment: Closest concept materially addresses the actual public bachelor identity: electrical/software intelligence, information acquisition/processing and connected/self-driving systems, not solely generic mathematics. Sustained perception, learned decision policies, computational motion/kinematics and signals models implement these subjects. Real product mechanisms/prototyping and life-cycle work connect to design trade-offs. Broad mathematics, algorithms, databases and operating systems have specific modelling/information-infrastructure functions, not invented automotive syllabi. Robotics sensing/control is not inflated beyond its smaller role. Description-only RL/database/advanced-calculus/renewable-system courses receive full supported weight. The physical-engineering gaps remain substantial but are not a quota or equivalence test; unlike a mechanically organised target, this target explicitly foregrounds electronics/software and connected intelligence. The sustainable variant is strengthened with actual conversion/storage/grid/yield work replacing climate context, with physical/material foundations and resource recovery, not a battery-specialist promise. It meets qualitative and five-course distinctness. Further mechanical/propulsion direction fails sustained content, not missing planning coverage.
